notes: ACTIVE relation pack (upgraded from pilot). No invented Sn/Sp. Traditional MTrP maps labeled traditional — not absolute anatomy. No Travell verbatim text. Companion MD: clinical-reasoning/cervical-referred-differential.md, evidence/relations-cervical.md, evidence/referred-pain-cervical.md.

relations.source_structure: cervical somatic / nerve root structures (C5–C7 pathway clinical)
relations.clinical_context: Scapular or shoulder-girdle pain with neck movement contribution, dermatomal clues, or weak local shoulder reproduction.
supporting_evidence: Neck Pain CPGs endorse cervical contribution to upper quarter symptoms
Wainner cluster supports radiculopathy when present; somatic referral also common

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Cannot localize exact cervical segment from scapular pain alone.

recommended_examination: Cervical AROM + Spurling / distraction / ULTT as cluster
Ask if neck movement changes scapular/shoulder pain
Local shoulder cluster for familiar pain
red_flags: Canadian C-spine rule indications after trauma

references.citation: Blanpied PR et al. Neck Pain: Revision 2017 (CPG). JOSPT.
Wainner RS et al. Reliability and diagnostic accuracy of the clinical examination for cervical radiculopathy. Spine.

relations.clinical_context: Axial or scapular pain changing with cervical extension/rotation; non-dermatomal pattern.
supporting_evidence: Dwyer/Aprill/Bogduk and Fukui provocation maps show shoulder-girdle referral from cervical facets
Experimental maps ≠ office test that names a segment

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Not Sn/Sp of Kemp-like maneuvers or palpation.

limitations: Cannot diagnose 'C5 facet' from a pain drawing

references.citation: Dwyer A, Aprill C, Bogduk N. Cervical zygapophyseal joint pain patterns. Spine. 1990.
Fukui S et al. Referred pain distribution of the cervical zygapophyseal joints. Pain. 1996.

relations.clinical_context: Neck-related arm pain ± paresthesia; may mimic peripheral entrapment or local elbow/wrist pain.
supporting_evidence: Wainner cluster and Neck Pain CPG support radicular patterns
Dermatomes are approximate, not absolute maps

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Cluster > single test; do not invent root-level certainty from pain location alone.

limitations: Overlap with CTS / cubital tunnel / LET
alternative_explanations: Somatic referred pain without frank radiculopathy
recommended_examination: Peripheral provocation as adjuncts (Phalen, elbow flexion)
Do not auto-label CTS because hand tingles

references.citation: Wainner RS et al. Spine. 2003.
Blanpied PR et al. Neck Pain CPG. JOSPT. 2017.

relations.source_structure: upper cervical somatic structures (C1–C3 clinical construct)
relations.clinical_context: Unilateral headache associated with neck movement/posture after SNOOP/red-flag screen.
supporting_evidence: Cervicogenic headache is a clinical pattern overlapping primary headache
No isolated MSK test proves cervicogenic headache

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Overlap with migraine/TTH; qualitative pattern only.

limitations: Must screen secondary headache red flags first
recommended_examination: Cervical AROM and upper cervical assessment as tolerated
Do not invent Sn/Sp for flexion-rotation test as absolute

references.citation: Bogduk N, Govind J. Cervicogenic headache: an assessment of the evidence. Lancet Neurol. 2009.
Blanpied PR et al. Neck Pain CPG. JOSPT. 2017.

relations.clinical_context: Arm pain, paresthesia, or scapular pain with cervical history but Spurling negative.
supporting_evidence: Spurling often described as more specific than sensitive
Wainner cluster outperforms single tests

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Negative Spurling does not exclude cervical radiculopathy. Do not invent Sn/Sp.

alternative_explanations: Cervical somatic referred pain without radiculopathy
recommended_examination: Repeat under lower irritability if needed

references.citation: Tong HC, Haig AJ, Yamakawa K. The Spurling test and cervical radiculopathy. Spine.
Wainner RS et al. Spine.

relations.source_structure: upper limb neural continuum (median/radial/ulnar biased variants)
relations.clinical_context: Suspected neurodynamic or radicular contribution; ULTT negative or only stretch without familiar symptoms.
supporting_evidence: Neurodynamic tests require familiar symptom reproduction for clinical meaning
Component of Wainner cluster — not standalone exclusion

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Reliability and accuracy vary by variant and population; qualitative limitations only.

recommended_examination: Do not auto-switch to MTrP because ULTT is negative

references.citation: Wainner RS et al. Cervical radiculopathy clinical examination. Spine.
Blanpied PR et al. Neck Pain CPG. JOSPT.

relations.clinical_context: Load-related shoulder pain plus neck symptoms, dual reproduction on cervical and cuff testing.
supporting_evidence: Clinical coexistence is common; treating one region alone may fail
Negative Spurling does not rule out dual contribution

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Coexistence is clinical reasoning, not a single accuracy metric.

limitations: Do not force a single-label diagnosis
Prioritize red flags and neurological deficit first
recommended_examination: Document which tests reproduce familiar pain in which region
Treat/reevaluate the dominant reproducible driver first

references.citation: Lewis J. Rotator cuff related shoulder pain — assessment uncertainties and cervical screen framing.
Blanpied PR et al. Neck Pain CPG. JOSPT.

relations.clinical_context: Interscapular or mid-back pain with neck contribution; thoracic mechanical pain may coexist.
supporting_evidence: Cross-region cervicothoracic screening is standard when scapular pain is poorly localized
Thoracic-specific evidence for treatment is limited (OPTIMa/Briganti themes)

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Do not invent a thoracic facet level from interscapular pain.

limitations: Visceral red flags must be screened for mid-back/chest patterns
Evidence for isolated thoracic labeling is limited

references.citation: Blanpied PR et al. Neck Pain CPG. JOSPT. 2017.
Briganti / OPTIMa thoracic pain evidence themes — limited treatment certainty.

relations.clinical_context: Suspected radiculopathy: use a cluster (rotation limitation, Spurling, distraction, ULTT) plus neuro screen — not one test.
supporting_evidence: Wainner cluster improves clinical reasoning vs isolated tests
Familiar symptom reproduction required for meaning

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Cite cluster qualitatively; do not invent numeric LR for the whole battery in-app.

limitations: Does not replace imaging when management changes

references.citation: Wainner RS et al. Spine. 2003.

relations.clinical_context: Postural load / shoulder hiking; palpation may reproduce familiar pain — hypothesis only after articular/neural screen.
supporting_evidence: Traditional myofascial maps describe neck/head/shoulder patterns (traditional class only)
limitations: Must not replace SNOOP or radiculopathy reasoning

references.citation: Tough EA et al. 2007 — MTrP diagnostic criteria variability / caution.
Lucas N et al. Clin J Pain. 2009 — palpation reliability caution.

relations.clinical_context: Sustained postures / unilateral load; familiar pain on palpation only — traditional hypothesis.
supporting_evidence: Traditional maps describe superior scapular angle patterns

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Do not treat as proven generator.

recommended_examination: Familiar-pain palpation as weak adjunct only

references.citation: Tough EA et al. 2007; Lucas N et al. 2009 — methodological caution for MTrP.

relations.target_region: hands / gait / bilateral upper and lower limbs
relations.clinical_context: Neck pain or upper limb symptoms plus gait disturbance, hand clumsiness, hyperreflexia, or Hoffman/Babinski-type concerns.
supporting_evidence: Neck Pain CPGs list myelopathy features as indications for medical referral / imaging pathways

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Individual myelopathy signs imperfect; act on constellation. No invented Sn/Sp.

recommended_examination: Neurological screen upper and lower limbs
Urgent referral per local pathway — stop elective hypothesis cascade

references.citation: Blanpied PR et al. Neck Pain: Revision 2017 (CPG). JOSPT — myelopathy / referral criteria framing.
Cook C et al. Clustered clinical findings for cervical myelopathy — qualitative use of clusters, not single tests.

relations.clinical_context: Blunt trauma to neck/head with Canadian C-Spine Rule (or local equivalent) indications — imaging/medical pathway before elective MSK care.
supporting_evidence: Canadian C-Spine Rule is a validated decision rule for imaging after trauma in appropriate settings

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Use rule qualitatively in-app; do not restate full numeric performance as invented certainty for every context.

recommended_examination: Stop elective cervical mobilization/testing if rule positive or unstable risk
red_flags: Inability to actively rotate as defined by rule

references.citation: Stiell IG et al. The Canadian C-Spine Rule for radiography in alert and stable trauma patients. JAMA. 2001.
Blanpied PR et al. Neck Pain CPG — trauma / referral framing. JOSPT.
